title: OpenIE Database & Data Desk: Sub-Microsecond Memory-Mapped Stores and Hash-Chained Logs
subtitle: Cecily, Marcus, and Kwame examine 1.77 uJ DNULLMM1 POSIX mmap case stores, RCE-VC name-free logs, and bit-exact replay across macOS, Linux, and Windows
summary: At the OpenIE Database & Data Desk (database.openie.dev / data.openie.dev), Cecily, Marcus, and Kwame tour 35.28M data cells, 0.325 us / 1.77 uJ DNULLMM1 POSIX mmap and Win32 MapViewOfFile case stores, 69.7 us RCE-VC name-free versioned logs, and zero-diff deterministic replay across macOS, Linux, and bare-metal Windows 11.

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Fourteen — our OpenIE Database and Data Desk roundtable on OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Cecily, joined by Marcus and Kwame — three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced via ElevenLabs studio neural speech and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we open database.openie.dev and data.openie.dev!

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: Picture two ways to check a subway transfer as train doors close: mail a handwritten YAML letter to a warehouse clerk, or glance up at a laminated map bolted right onto the station wall!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Most agent memory stacks picked the handwritten YAML letter! In AI Reads Human, pure-Python YAML burned two thousand fifty-three times more energy per record than fixed binary structs. Kwame, how does DNULLMM1 bolt the map straight onto the CPU?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: DNULLMM1 packs a sixty-four-byte header plus forty-eight-byte open-addressed binary hash slots and mounts them zero-copy via POSIX mmap on Linux and macOS or MapViewOfFile on Windows 11. Zero parsing, zero heap allocation: one lookup finishes in zero point three two five microseconds at one point seven seven microjoules!

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: How do database.openie.dev's thirty-five point two eight million data cells connect to state.openie.dev and memory.openie.dev?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Across ten database axes and five hundred thirty-three million memory cells from CPU registers to DNA, every table view is a deterministic fold over an append-only, hash-chained bitemporal log — separating Valid Time in reality from Transaction Time in the chain so history is never overwritten.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What happens when ten coding agents commit to one repository at once? Standard Git line-number merges turn into gridlock!

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: RCE-VC keys every definition by its canonical name-free digest! Non-overlapping edits need zero coordination: admitting a submission against one hundred thousand units takes sixty-nine point seven to seventy-three point six microseconds at three hundred seventeen to three hundred sixty-five microjoules of Apple M5 Max L3 reported_j, while projecting cleanly back to Git!

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: Now test cross-platform deterministic replay across macOS, Linux, and bare-metal Windows 11 — where do ordinary systems drift?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Windows NTFS carriage-return line-feeds corrupt naive text transcripts, and standard-library floating-point sine diverges across Apple libSystem, Linux glibc, and Windows UCRT in just ten to thirty-seven ticks!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And when you ran frozen binary DNULLMM1 maps plus Q32.32 fixed-point integer state across all those machines?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: All five SATB hardware and OS hosts hit the exact ten-thousand-probe checksum fifteen billion twenty-seven million seven hundred five thousand seven hundred thirty-six with zero byte diffs! And in GE-H8, three one-hour sessions of two hundred sixteen thousand ticks replayed bit-for-bit across macOS, Linux, and Windows 11 from forty-four point six kilobytes of gzipped inputs — zero out of six thousand four hundred eighty mismatches!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Final audit check: how do we stop test-time mutation or solver smuggling inside DNULLMM1 and RCE-VC?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Before testing, DNULLMM1 is frozen read-only by SHA-256 under Bitcoin OpenTimestamps and drand beacons — pre-and-post digests must match with zero test writes, and reducers are capped at four thousand ninety-six gzipped bytes and fifty thousand operations! Meanwhile, RCE-VC refuses overlapping edits with a recorded reason and keeps measured_j unset alongside reported_j.

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: Hash-chain the bitemporal log, memory-map verified state at one point seven seven microjoules, and replay bit-for-bit everywhere! Explore all six openie.dev desks right below, subscribe via Podcast RSS, and thank you for listening to OpenIE Research Radio!
